trigger_or_context: A hard or touchy thing comes up in the relationship that needs to be talked about.
short_term_function: Bringing it up means the hard stuff gets talked about instead of being ignored.
developmental_cost: You carry the whole job of starting hard talks. Your partner never has to, so you can't see if they would step up too. Doing it alone can wear you down.
adaptive_alternative_1: Keep bringing up things that matter. But once, name the pattern out loud. Tell your partner you'd like the job of starting hard talks to be shared. Then leave a little room and watch if they ever start one too.
what_new_response_supports: You find out if your partner can carry some of this too, or if it always falls on you.
expected_discomfort_or_cost: Some hard things may sit a bit longer while you wait to see if they speak up. Holding back can feel uncomfortable.
context_conditions: Bringing up hard things is healthy — this is not about going quiet. It is about whether you are always the only one. If a real problem needs to be raised now, raise it.
review_reason: Context-dependent behavior; the short-term function and the competency mapping both needed judgment.
